meta.tagline: Freedom, canals, and more bicycles than people

overview.title: Welcome to Amsterdam
overview.intro: The moment you step off the train, Amsterdam hits different. The houses lean sideways — yes, on purpose, they're 17th century and proud of it. The canals wind through the city like a maze. And somehow the whole place just feels free.

local_word.definition: That warm, cozy, can't-quite-translate-it Dutch vibe — sitting by the water with a coffee, watching boats drift past. This single word explains the soul of Amsterdam. You'll feel it everywhere.

rules.title: Never walk on the red bike paths
rules.description: Cyclists own this city and they will not stop for you. Step onto a bike lane = instant danger. The number one tourist mistake in Amsterdam.

rules.title: Amsterdam runs on cards, not cash
rules.description: From tiny bakeries to street markets, most places are card-only. Don't be surprised by the 'Card Only' sign — just tap and go.

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: Tap in AND tap out on trams

tip.label: Local tip
tip.text: When you find a cosy brown café on a rainy afternoon, order a beer and just sit — that's gezellig in action. No agenda. No rush. Just Amsterdam.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: In Amsterdam, how you move is part of the experience. Get this right and the city opens up completely.

items.title: Airport → City Center
items.description: The simplest option is the train. Schiphol has its own station directly below the terminal — take the escalators down with your luggage and board. Trains to Amsterdam Centraal run every 10–15 minutes and take 15–20 minutes. Fast, cheap, and stress-free. Taxis and transfer services cost 4–5 times more and are subject to traffic.

items.title: Bicycle — the city's real lifeblood
items.description: Rent one and Amsterdam suddenly makes sense. Three golden rules: never walk on the red bike lanes; always use two locks — bike theft here is practically a local sport; never stop in the middle of a bike lane to take a photo. Other cyclists won't warn you, they'll just ride past.

items.title: Trams, Buses & Metro
items.description: Trams are the backbone of the city, gliding through narrow streets to reach everywhere. Tap your OV-chipkaart or phone when boarding AND when exiting. Missing the exit tap gets processed as a maximum fare by the system. Everyone makes this mistake at the beginning.

items.title: Free Ferries to Noord
items.description: Free ferries depart continuously from directly behind Centraal Station to Amsterdam Noord — free for pedestrians, cyclists and mopeds. Short, breezy, and a small experience in itself. Runs all day and into the night.

items.title: Taxi & Uber
items.description: Both options exist but cost 4–5 times more than public transport. Worth considering for late nights or special situations — not as daily transport. Uber works smoothly in Amsterdam.

callout.label: Shoe tip
callout.text: Wear comfortable, flat shoes. Canal-side stones are uneven and slippery. When crossing any street — look for bikes first, cars second. The bicycle army is silent and fast.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: Your neighborhood shapes your whole trip. The Centrum is overpriced and loud — step one ring out and Amsterdam gets real.

local_word.definition: The sacred Dutch after-work ritual — beer, bitterballen, and an afternoon that goes nowhere in particular. Choosing a neighbourhood in Amsterdam means choosing where your Borrel happens. Find the right one and the right bruin café is just around the corner.

items.name: Jordaan
items.description: The most 'Amsterdam' neighbourhood that exists. Narrow alleys, ivy-covered canal houses, boutique hotels right on the water. Buildings are 400 years old — expect very steep stairs and tiny rooms. Bring a small suitcase.

items.name: De Pijp
items.description: Amsterdam's 'Latin Quarter.' Home to the Albert Cuypmarkt — the city's biggest open-air market — a buzzing student scene, and restaurants from every corner of the world. Slightly cheaper than center, way more alive.

items.name: Grachtengordel (Canal Belt)
items.description: Living inside a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Grand, high-ceilinged canal houses that end up on every postcard. Walking distance to everything, but expect tourist crowds on weekends.

items.name: Oud-West
items.description: The local's secret. Home to De Hallen — a gorgeous food hall and cinema in a converted tram depot — walking distance to Vondelpark. Best value-for-money area in Amsterdam. 10 minutes to center by tram.

items.name: Amsterdam Noord
items.description: Across the free ferry behind Central Station. Former shipyards turned cool hotels, massive street art murals, digital nomad hub. Completely different energy. Catch the NDSM flea market on weekends.

best_time.title: Best Time to Visit
best_time.intro: Amsterdam isn't a 'one perfect time' city — it's a 'depends what you're after' city.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Tulip Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Most Iconic
items.description: Keukenhof Gardens explodes with millions of tulips. Then April 27th — King's Day — the entire city turns orange, every street becomes a party, and the canals fill with boats. One of the biggest street celebrations in Europe. If you can only go once, make it spring.

callout.label: Don't miss
callout.text: King's Day (April 27) — book accommodation months ahead. Streets become free markets and the whole city dances.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Long Days
items.subtitle: Summer · Most Social
items.description: Sun sets past 10 PM. Locals picnic on canal boats. Vondelpark buzzes with live music. But weather is unpredictable — warm morning? Bring a jacket anyway. Rain arrives without warning.

callout.label: Pack note
callout.text: Always carry a compact rain jacket, even in July. Amsterdam weather follows no logic.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Moody & Golden
items.subtitle: Autumn · Most Atmospheric
items.description: Canal trees turn amber and orange, the city gets its famous melancholic, moody beauty. October brings Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE) — the whole city becomes the world's electronic music capital. Gezellig spirit peaks: rainy evenings, warm brown cafes, locals actually home.

callout.label: Local word
callout.text: 'Bruin café' (brown café) — the dark wood-panelled pubs where gezellig truly lives. Find one in a rainstorm.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Canal Magic
items.subtitle: Winter · Most Magical
items.description: Quieter, mistier, and honestly magical. The Amsterdam Light Festival transforms the canals into an open-air art museum. And if you get very lucky — rare, but it happens — the canals freeze and locals ice skate on them.

callout.label: Insider
callout.text: Frozen canals happen maybe once a decade. Follow local Amsterdam news in January — if it happens, drop everything and go.

monthly_highlights.text: Keukenhof is open (late Mar–mid May) — the heart of tulip season, a half-day trip from Amsterdam.
Koningsdag (King's Day): the whole city turns orange and the canals become one big boat party. Either dive all the way in, or don't be in town that day.
Grachtenfestival: classical music on the canals, many concerts free. Pride canal parade in the first week.
Amsterdam Light Festival: the canals fill with light installations, best seen from a boat.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Dutch food is better than its reputation. Some of this you can only find here.

local_word.definition: Cheers! Say it when your beer arrives during a Borrel — Amsterdam's sacred after-work drinking ritual. Followed immediately by bitterballen.

items.name: Vlaamse Frites + Patat Oorlog
items.description: Thick-cut, double-fried, in a paper cone. Order Patat Oorlog (War Fries): peanut sauce, mayo, and raw onion. Sounds chaotic. Tastes incredible.

items.name: Stroopwafel — fresh, not packaged
items.description: Two thin waffle layers with caramel in the middle. Get one warm from Albert Cuypmarkt. The supermarket versions don't compare.

items.name: Dutch Cheese (Kaas)
items.description: You're in Gouda country. Cheese shops offer free tastings — aged, young, smoked, herb-infused. Try Henri Willig or Old Amsterdam. Always free to taste.

items.name: Bitterballen + Borrel
items.description: Fried crispy balls filled with creamy meat ragout, dipped in mustard. Always eaten alongside an afternoon beer — that's the Borrel, Amsterdam's after-work ritual. Any brown café.

items.name: Haring (Raw Herring)
items.description: Hold by the tail, tilt back, lower it in — that's the traditional way. Too bold? Get a broodje haring with pickles and onion. Either way, try it once.

items.name: Rijsttafel — Indonesian Feast
items.description: 15–20 small Indonesian dishes served together — rich, spiced, completely unlike anything else in Amsterdam. The most delicious remnant of Dutch colonial history. Reserve an evening.

items.name: Poffertjes
items.description: Tiny, fluffy mini-pancakes dusted with powdered sugar and butter. A childhood favourite in the Netherlands. Find them at any street market.

callout.label: Late night secret
callout.text: Find a FEBO automat — tap your card at a wall of little glass windows and pull out a hot kroket. Amsterdam's oldest fast-food tradition. Completely unique after midnight.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: The real Amsterdam is behind doors, down alleys, and across free ferries. Most tourists walk right past these.

items.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder — Church in an Attic
items.description: From the outside: a normal canal house. Inside, hidden on the top floor: a fully intact 17th-century Catholic church. Built secretly when Catholic worship was banned. Amsterdam's most powerful symbol of tolerance — almost nobody knows it's there.

items.name: Begijnhof — The Hidden Courtyard
items.description: A medieval courtyard behind an unmarked door on Spui square. Step through and the noise disappears entirely. Built in the 14th century. No sign on the door — look for a small wooden gate in the wall.

items.name: Tuschinski Theater
items.description: One of the most beautiful Art Deco buildings in the world. Even if you don't watch a film, walk into the lobby. Carpets, ceiling, chandeliers — a time machine to 1921 Amsterdam. Most tourists walk past and never go inside.

items.name: NDSM Werf + Weekend Flea Market
items.description: Old shipyard turned street art wonderland via the free ferry. Giant scrap metal sculptures, massive murals. On weekends: the NDSM flea market brings artists, food trucks, and vintage stalls. The Amsterdam of the future.

items.name: Hofjes — Secret Garden Courts
items.description: Amsterdam has dozens of hidden gardens behind unmarked wooden doors. Begijnhof is the famous one, but Jordaan has several others — Karthuizerhofje, Sint Andrieshofje. Follow small signs on walls. Step through and find a garden 400 years removed from the city outside.

items.name: Winkel 43 — The Apple Pie Pilgrimage
items.description: Thick, cinnamon-heavy, served warm with a mountain of fresh whipped cream (slagroom). Queue is worth every minute. Go for afternoon coffee on a rainy day.

callout.label: De Wallen rule
callout.text: Do NOT photograph the windows in the Red Light District. Illegal, deeply disrespectful, hostile response guaranteed. Phone stays in pocket — no exceptions.

items.label: Sit by a canal at sunset
items.sub: Jordaan or Prinsengracht — feet over the edge, beer in hand

items.label: Visit the Anne Frank House
items.sub: Book 2–3 months ahead. No walk-ins. Worth every step.

items.label: Get lost in the 9 Straatjes
items.sub: Nine Streets — vintage shops, boutiques, hidden gems. Budget extra time.

items.label: Peek into the Rijksmuseum's Cuypers Library
items.sub: Even if you skip the galleries — the architecture will stop you

items.label: Take the free ferry to Amsterdam Noord
items.sub: Behind Centraal Station — free, 5 minutes, completely different world

items.label: Browse the Bloemenmarkt
items.sub: World's only floating flower market. Tulip bulbs to actually take home.

items.label: Do a canal tour at golden hour
items.sub: The light on canal houses one hour before sunset is unlike anything else

items.label: Have a Borrel with bitterballen
items.sub: Any brown café, any afternoon. Bitterballen + beer. Say Proost!

items.label: Experience a FEBO moment
items.sub: Late night automat wall — kroket from a little glass window

items.label: Walk through Begijnhof
items.sub: Find the unmarked door on Spui square. Step through. Breathe.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Amsterdam is not ruthless about tourist traps, but the center has a few classics. Know them, and spend your money and time on the real Amsterdam.

items.name: Photo-menu restaurants on Damrak and Leidseplein
items.description: The neon-lit places that greet you off the train, with a waiter at the door and a menu in 12 languages. Overpriced, mediocre, and where no Dutch person ever sits.
items.instead: Walk two streets in: in Jordaan or De Pijp the same money buys a meal twice as good.

items.name: Giant glass-covered canal boats
items.description: The big boats hauling 70 people with a recorded audio guide show you the canals without letting you feel them. Even photos are hard through the glass.
items.instead: Pick a small open boat with a live skipper — and time it for sunset.

items.name: Souvenir cheese and tulip shops on Damrak
items.description: Vacuum-packed 'Gouda' and tulip bulbs that will never bloom. Inflated prices, low quality, and much of it isn't even locally made.
items.instead: Buy cheese at a real kaas shop after tasting; get certified (customs-approved) bulbs at Bloemenmarkt stalls.

items.name: Taxi from Schiphol to the city
items.description: You'll pay €60–70 and take twice as long as the train in traffic. The airport taxi queue is Amsterdam's most expensive waiting room.
items.instead: The train reaches Centraal in 15–20 minutes; the platforms are right below the terminal.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: If someone at the door is calling you inside, the place can't sell itself. Good spots in Amsterdam never call you — you find them.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: The classics + a taste of the real Amsterdam

steps.title: Breakfast in Jordaan
steps.description: Start the day with apple pie at Winkel 43 — yes, pie for breakfast, you're here.

steps.title: 9 Straatjes + Canal Belt walk
steps.description: From the Nine Streets south along Prinsengracht; don't rush, stop on the bridges.

steps.title: Lunch at Albert Cuypmarkt
steps.description: A warm stroopwafel, fresh haring, or whatever calls you. Standing up, market style.

steps.title: Rijksmuseum or Van Gogh
steps.description: Don't cram both into one day. Pick one and take your time. Book the ticket ahead.

steps.title: Borrel at a bruin café
steps.description: Bitterballen + beer. The most Dutch hour of the day.

steps.title: Canalside at sunset
steps.description: Grab a bottle of something from a market, sit on the canal edge, let your feet dangle. The whole day was for this.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the city as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: The center and the classics
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Jordaan, canals, one big museum, borrel.

steps.title: Noord and alternative Amsterdam
steps.description: Take the free ferry to Noord: NDSM, street art, A'DAM tower. In the afternoon, Anne Frank House (book months ahead!) and dinner in De Pijp.

steps.title: Hidden Amsterdam + one last gezellig
steps.description: Begijnhof, Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder, the hofjes courtyards. A small-boat canal cruise in the afternoon, and a rijsttafel farewell feast at night.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Everyone speaks English, but even a single word of Dutch changes faces.

items.meaning: Thank you — the word you'll use most
Please / here you go — also said when handing something over
Cheers! Don't forget the eye contact
Tasty / great — works for food and for the weather
Bye — cheerful, said twice: doei doei!
